newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav wheat planting on schedule - farm ministry.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav wheat planting on schedule - farm ministry.

text.p: Yugoslavia's agriculture ministry is satisfied with the pace of autumn wheat sowing despite a constant lack of funds, a senior ministry official said on Thursday.
"The autumn wheat sowing is going according to the plan," Milan Prostran of the agriculture ministry told Reuters. "Our plan to sow 850,000 hectares with wheat this fall will be achieved."
Last year only 410,000 ha of wheat were sown by mid-November down from 650,000 a year earlier.
By November 11 wheat had been down on 721,000 ha, up from 572,000 just a week earlier. According to Prostran, 22,000-25,000 ha are being sown each day.

If good weather continued, the ministry expected agricultural work to be completed on time. "We are very happy with the dynamic of wheat sowing this year," he said, adding that interest among farmers was high.
To overcome a shortage of cash for autumn sowing, the government had issued wheat forward contracts for advanced purchase of up to 1.2 million tonnes of the 1997 wheat crop.
It also financed another 192,000 tonnes of wheat through barter arrangements, with farmers paid in kind -- wheat seed, fertiliser and diesel.
Prostran said Yugoslavia could easily sow one million hectares to wheat in future and become a significant exporter.
Only 582,965 ha of wheat were sown last year, when output totalled 1.71 million tonnes.
